key_insight: Epitaxial α-MnTe thin films on InP(111) show transport signatures consistent with a finite net magnetic polarization, despite bulk MnTe being a compensated antiferromagnet.
engineering_relevance: This suggests thin-film epitaxy and microstructure control can be used to engineer magnetic responses for future spintronic devices.
method: Molecular beam epitaxy grew α-MnTe films on InP(111).
Low-temperature magneto-transport measured hysteretic longitudinal magnetoresistance and nonlinear transverse magnetoresistance.
DFT was used to probe interface and defect-driven routes to emergent magnetization.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a distinct hysteretic butterfly longitudinal magnetoresistance and nonlinear transverse magnetoresistance as experimental evidence, supported by DFT mechanisms for finite magnetization in thin films.
watch_item: The inferred magnetic polarization is indirect from transport and may depend strongly on interface symmetry breaking, defects, and film quality.
paper_title: Transport Evidence of Magnetic Polarization in the Altermagnetic Candidate MnTe
